summary: Built 1916 on Mount Watatic (Ashburnham/Ashby, MA); hurricanes felled towers in 1938 and 1950, closed 1979, removed and sold 1996; summit now conservation land.

facts.design: Original tower of 40 or 48 ft with fire-escape stairs; steel Aermotor-style tower from 1939, replaced by an Aermotor MC-39 style tower in 1951
facts.status_note: Tower taken down and sold in 1996; no source describes what remains of the footings.

staffing.status: Staffed; closed after the 1979 fire season

access.note: Summit is protected conservation land crossed by the Wapack and Midstate trails; no tower stands to climb.

visit.trail_note: The Wapack Trail and the Midstate Trail both cross the mountain.

events.note: Under construction by June 1916 and erected that season per the 1917 state report; firetower.org dates it 1917.
Lookout in charge of the station; season finished by October.
Original tower destroyed in the Great New England Hurricane, September 1938.
Steel Aermotor-style replacement built by Civilian Conservation Corps crews.
Ashburnham forest fire: lookout reported it under control in April; AP reports said 2,000 more acres burned. It flared again in September, according to word from the tower.
Steel tower blown down and destroyed in a hurricane wind.
New Aermotor MC-39 style tower built.
Closed at the end of the 1979 fire season.
Tower removed and sold to a Connecticut resident.
Summit sold to Industrial Communications and Electronics for a planned 150-foot cellular tower and access road.
Ashby Land Trust, Ashburnham Conservation Trust, both towns and two state agencies bought the mountain for $2,500,000; about 281 acres protected.
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register as US 2, MA 2.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firetower.org gives the original tower as 48 feet; the State Forester report of 1917 gives 40 feet. The record keeps 12.2 m (40 ft) from the state report.

firetower.org dates the original build to 1917; a June 1916 newspaper item says it was under construction and the 1917 state report says it was erected during the past season. The build event is dated 1916.
firetower.org says one mile of phone line; the 1917 state report says two miles.

notes_for_editor: Brief said access unknown; set to public because the summit is conservation land crossed by trails. Sources disagree on the build year (1916 vs 1917), height (40 vs 48 ft) and phone line length (1 vs 2 miles). No source describes the footings today. Forest Lookouts is a compilation of newspaper and state-report quotes; Wikipedia is used for its own statements. Unread lead: ffla.org/lookouts/ma/ashburnham.htm. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the 1913 newspaper item names the company as Crocker, Burbank & Co. and gives no location, so the story no longer calls it local. The 2002 buyers are from the full Wikipedia sentence.
